html:
Browser task queues and dependency intent

The browser captures user intent and displays accepted work. The server owns execution eligibility, task order, continuation creation and results. Closing a page does not stop an accepted task or its queues. This guide follows the desktop conversation queue, its dependency selector and the shared continuation panel. The mobile conversation composer has a separate implementation; the continuation panel is shared between shells. See mobile task submission and queue sheets for its capture, retry and mounted-sheet boundaries.

Two queue identities matter. A conversation task is accepted through POST /api/agent/conversation-tasks and belongs to a conversation lane. A queued continuation belongs to an existing task lineage and uses /api/agent/native/{request_id}/follow-up-queue. For the server transactions, retry digests, execution limits and recovery rules, see the authoritative conversation coordinator and follow-up queue guides. For the inline instruction editor that sends continuations and steering, see instruction editor flows.

Owners and data flow

Implementation Responsibility
prompt_queue.js Captures submissions, preserves uncertain retry bodies, projects lane rows and sends explicit queue actions.
task_dependencies.js Keeps a selected dependency stable across lane updates and restores it after a failed submission only while the selection still belongs to that submission.
conversation_snapshot.js Owns canonical selected-conversation reads, navigation fencing and conversion of indexed lanes to ordered task arrays.
app.js Supplies composer envelopes, provisional cards, acceptance callbacks, request observation and canonical snapshot application.
followup_queue.js Displays lineage queue summaries/items, coalesces detail reads and reconciles deletion races.
flowchart TD Composer[Composer text and accepted control values] --> Capture[Detached submission envelope] Dependency[Explicit Run After task identity] --> Capture Capture --> Pending[Page-local retry identity and exact body] Pending --> API[Conversation task and lane APIs] API --> Store[Server-owned task and lane records] Store --> Coordinator[Server coordinator and execution owners] Store --> Snapshot[Canonical conversation snapshot] Snapshot --> Queue[Ordered queue rows and dependency choices] Snapshot --> Turns[Provisional or retained task cards and request observers] Queue --> Actions[Explicit edit, reorder, delete or steering action] Actions --> API Instructions[Inline instruction editor] --> FollowAPI[Scoped continuation queue API] FollowAPI --> Lineage[Server-owned lineage queue] Lineage --> Coordinator Lineage --> Panel[Shared continuation panel] Coordinator --> Snapshot

The pending submission map is page memory. It is not the durable queue. The queue controller stores only disclosure preference through the UI session helper; it does not save queued prompts to browser storage. Its lifetime is the page, with no public disposal method or polling timer. The mounted continuation panel has a separate dispose() operation.

Conversation admission and uncertain delivery

enqueue clones JSON-shaped composer input and validates nonblank text, the 24,000-character bound and leading slash commands. It preserves valid text exactly. The server enforces the queued-task limit and the rest of admission.

The pending map key is the serialized captured envelope, including its original field order. An exact pending key reuses the client submission ID and body. Changing text or settings can select a new key; this is not semantic deduplication of arbitrary equivalent objects. Accepted tasks have their separate server retry identity contract.

sequenceDiagram participant U as Composer participant Q as Browser queue participant D as Dependency selector participant A as Task admission API participant V as Shell cards and observation U->>Q: Enqueue captured prompt and settings Q->>Q: Clone, validate and find or create pending identity Q->>V: Show provisional submission immediately Q->>D: Reset selection and obtain guarded restore callback Q->>Q: Join the local serial submission chain Q->>A: POST exact retained body and client submission ID alt Acknowledgement received A-->>Q: Accepted task identity and current state Q->>Q: Remove pending identity and failure record Q-->>U: Invoke acceptance callback Q->>V: Update card and start accepted-task observation if scope still matches Q->>Q: Request canonical reconciliation else HTTP 4xx A-->>Q: Rejected request Q->>Q: Discard pending retry identity Q->>D: Restore only if navigation and edit revision still match Q->>V: Report definite failure in the current scope else Network error or other API failure A--xQ: Acceptance cannot be confirmed Q->>Q: Retain the same identity and body for exact retry Q->>D: Attempt guarded restoration Q->>V: Report unconfirmed submission end

Each POST runs after the preceding local attempt settles, even if it failed. Before the first POST, an envelope without a conversation ID can adopt the conversation just created by an earlier submission, provided navigation has not changed. That adoption removes new-conversation policy defaults from the body. Once built, the retained body is reused unchanged.

The implementation classifies all HTTP 4xx responses as definite failures. Other errors retain retry identity. A successful acknowledgement remains successful if card updates or observation callbacks throw; the user is told that controls could not refresh. Reloading the page loses this local pending map, so the browser's exact-retry guarantee applies to the retained controller, not a reconstructed prompt after reload. Accepted server work still survives.

Submission failures keep a visible explanation in the conversation even when Show runtime issues is off. The card retains the server's specific reason, field validation messages, human-readable recovery steps, settings/help links, HTTP status and error reference. Technical details remain expandable. These client notices live in the current page view, not durable task history. Error notifications remain until dismissed; ordinary informational toasts still expire.

Network failures, malformed acknowledgements and server failures explain that acceptance is unknown. They keep the pending identity and advise retrying the same prompt and settings to reconcile it. Rendering an error never retries work or changes settings. Once that retry is acknowledged, the uncertain-submission notice is resolved and its old failure detail is removed.

Navigation increments the presentation generation and clears lane/recovery state. It does not cancel already queued POST work or erase uncertain submission bodies. Acceptance callbacks for the caller may still run; generation checks protect the queue's scoped presentation callbacks. This is distinct from cancelling work on the server.

Canonical reads and fallback lane recovery

The normal selected-conversation owner reads one compact conversation snapshot. laneView resolves its ordered task IDs through tasks_by_id, retaining server order and omitting missing IDs. The shell applies this adapted lane with promptQueue.applyLane. That method trusts its caller's fencing; it does not run fallback attachment recovery or compare versions itself.

flowchart TD Trigger[Queue start, action completion or update invalidation] --> Selected{Canonical conversation selected?} Selected -->|yes| Canonical[Shared selected-conversation refresh] Canonical --> Read[Read compact snapshot with dependency and observed identities] Read --> Fence{Same conversation and navigation generation?} Fence -->|no| Ignore[Ignore stale response] Fence -->|yes| Version{New snapshot version?} Version -->|yes| Apply[Adapt indexed lane and apply through shell] Version -->|no| Retain[Retain already-applied presentation] Apply --> Again{Invalidated while reading?} Retain --> Again Again -->|yes| Read Again -->|no| Current[Publish current freshness] Selected -->|no and ready| Fallback[Coalesced lane GET] Fallback --> LaneFence{Same scope and non-older lane version?} LaneFence -->|no| Ignore LaneFence -->|yes| Recover[Render lane and attach eligible request observers] Recover --> Trailing{Another reconcile requested?} Trailing -->|yes| Fallback Trailing -->|no| Done[Return recovery result]

The canonical owner aborts its previous read on selection change, fences responses and asynchronous application by generation, and retains the last coherent snapshot with stale/error feedback after failure. Repeated ordinary refreshes join the same read; an invalidation can request a trailing pass. It applies a new snapshot version, or reapplies when explicitly invalidated for presentation repair.

The fallback lane path is used when no canonical conversation is selected and the queue has started. It rejects lower lane versions and stale navigation results, but does not abort its transport. It recovers observers for active tasks and newly seen request IDs, including a short task that finished while another stayed active. A recovered-ID set prevents duplicate attachment; a failed callback removes the ID so a later reconciliation can retry. Observation attaches to an accepted request and never starts another task. A missing-lane 404 is quiet; other read failures show refresh feedback and return false.

Edits, order changes and steering

Ordinary queue actions share one busy gate. Enqueue has its own serial chain, so the browser busy gate is not a server concurrency lock. Queue edits fetch the full task first; the response is used only if its original row is still connected and the same task is still being edited. Background renders preserve that active textarea. Save validates text and PATCHes the task; Cancel edit only closes the editor. History completion in this field is described in prompt recall flows.

sequenceDiagram participant U as User participant Q as Queue controls participant A as Task or lane API participant R as Canonical read owner U->>Q: Choose edit, reorder, remove, clear or explicit start opt Edit queued prompt Q->>A: GET full task detail A-->>Q: Prompt and task detail Q->>Q: Check mounted row and editing identity U->>Q: Save validated replacement text end Q->>Q: Acquire ordinary-action busy gate Q->>A: Send action and required observed lane version alt Action accepted A-->>Q: Result Q->>Q: Exit edit mode else Conflict or other failure A-->>Q: Error Q-->>U: Display error and preserve server ownership end Q->>Q: Release busy gate Q->>R: Reconcile accepted server state R-->>Q: Current lane projection

Reorder sends the complete observed queued-ID order and lane version. Run next and Start task for a dependency-blocked task also send the observed version. The server advertises whether Run next is available and enforces execution slots even for explicit starts. Clear queue deletes queued intent for the selected conversation; it does not stop the active task. See the coordinator controls for server checks.

Steer current and Steer without interrupting require no explicit task dependencies, an active lane task and a steerable current status. For detailed rows the browser compares the represented envelopes, including targets, context and supported policy fields. This comparison is partial: it does not establish equality of every possible execution setting. Compact rows intentionally lack that envelope and leave compatibility to the server. The second button sends steering_mode: after_response; both actions use the task's steer-current endpoint. An error is followed by reconciliation, not an invented successful delivery or client-side removal.

Dependency selection and restoration

The selector offers server-provided candidates in descending creation order. It retains a previously chosen task when that task completes or leaves the active candidate set. Reads include dependency_task_id, allowing the server to return that retained target. An explicitly unresolved target is shown as Unavailable; it is not silently converted to independent work. A new palette selection must belong to the current candidate set and conversation.

sequenceDiagram participant S as Server lane projection participant D as Dependency selector participant U as User participant Q as Browser submission S->>D: Candidate tasks and selected-target projection D->>D: Retain selected identity and stable select/options U->>D: Select Run After task D->>D: Advance local selection revision Q->>D: Capture identity, then reset for this submission D-->>Q: Restoration closure bound to scope and revision alt Submission fails while selection is unchanged and empty Q->>D: Invoke restoration closure D->>D: Restore exact selected identity else User changes selection or navigates U->>D: New intent or conversation D->>D: Advance revision or scope Q->>D: Invoke old restoration closure after failure D->>D: Leave newer intent untouched end

Task titles and dependency explanations are rendered as text. Unchanged options retain their DOM, and the selector stays enabled while focused even if its last candidate disappears. The Run After chip clears selection explicitly. Dependency events are emitted when the projected scope, selection or available tasks change; they do not schedule work. Blocker descriptions can include a direct target, an upstream target, skipped dependencies and archived status, using server facts.

Continuation panel reads, deletion and disposal

The continuation panel is mounted for a request ID, while its queue identity is the root lineage returned by the server. Its expansion map is shared within the page by root ID, so a later attempt can retain disclosure preference. It does not persist across page reloads.

sequenceDiagram participant N as Native snapshot owner participant P as Continuation panel participant A as Scoped queue API participant U as User N->>P: Root, revision, count, status and continuation marker P->>P: Project summary and hide superseded attempt controls U->>P: Open queue disclosure P->>A: Coalesced GET for full items A-->>P: Root and revision with public item labels P->>P: Ignore disposed or older same-root response U->>P: Delete an item marked deletable P->>A: DELETE selected item alt Deletion accepted A-->>P: Updated queue snapshot P->>P: Accept revision and restore owned keyboard focus else Scheduler already claimed the item A-->>P: HTTP 409 P-->>U: Report that continuation was already scheduled P->>A: Refresh actual queue A-->>P: Current snapshot end N->>P: Dispose mounted task view P->>P: Remove disclosure and panel, fence late read responses

Native summaries update count/status; an open panel refreshes full items when the status changes or the summary revision advances beyond the last accepted full read. Item rows rebuild only when their serialized item snapshot changes. Reads share an in-flight operation and can request a trailing pass. Same-root older responses are ignored; equal revisions are accepted, and a different root has its own revision sequence.

Delete buttons follow each item's can_delete. A 409 reports a scheduling race; other failures offer retry feedback. Both failure paths refresh rather than pretending the item disappeared. Successful deletion restores focus only when the deleted control owned focus and the panel has not been disposed. Resource names, Gateway labels and parameter keys are public text; private parameter values are not rendered here.

Closing the disclosure removes read feedback but does not cancel the HTTP request. Disposal fences late response painting and removes the panel; it does not cancel accepted server intent or abort transport. An attempt marked continued_by hides its old queue controls. The panel's enqueue sends the caller's supplied identity and resources; uncertain-submission retry ownership remains with the instruction editor.

Evidence and scope

The queue, desktop dependency selector and shared continuation panel were reviewed in full. The snapshot reader and shell integrations were reviewed only at the boundaries described here. The evidence includes deterministic browser fixtures in dependency controls, conversation queue actions, continuation panels and concurrent task observation. These fixtures use local state and intercepted APIs. They exercise browser behavior, not live model execution or a real Gateway. The review ledger records the selected cases and their results separately from full server contracts.
